d: an altar with a base or pedestal; for offering sacrifices to a god
a relatively large and elaborate seat upon which a ruler sits on official occasions
a relatively small altar used for burning incense; made of wood

any type of altar or object where gifts may be placed and ritual observances carried out in honor of supernatural beings (in the NT θυσιαστήριον is employed to refer to a number of different types of altars; including the altar for burnt offerings in the Temple; the altar of incense; the altar which Abraham built; and the heavenly altar mentioned in the book of Revelation)
a piece of furniture used for sitting; differs widely in shape and materials; often made of a wooden or cane frame with the seat woven of reeds or made of wood; with or without a back
a relatively small and often temporary type of object on which a person may lie or recline; made of reeds or cloth; thin and light for carrying

a piece of furniture used for sleeping

an object, usually soft, on which one may lay one’s head
a stretcher or plank used for carrying a corpse to a place of burial
a generic expression for any type of table
a piece of furniture on which one may rest one’s feet
